title: Working at Redwood: Careers, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, Internal Tools
author: Alex Kim
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood's canonical employee-facing guidance for: what it's like to work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders across major functions, core benefits and perks, the standard hiring and onboarding process, and the internal tools new hires will use.

Use this page as the single-source reference for people-ops, hiring managers, and new hires. For function-specific career ladders (e.g., Research, Infra, Product), see the linked pages in Related pages.

1) Working at Redwood — our culture and expectations

Intro
- Mission-aligned: we prioritize shipping reliable, cost-conscious inference infrastructure and developer ergonomics.
- Engineering-first: technical rigor, blameless postmortems, and strong documentation are core behaviors.
- Customer-focused: product decisions are informed by real workloads and SLO-driven tradeoffs.

Core behaviors we expect from every Redwooder
- Ownership: own the outcome, not just the task.
- Communication: clear async updates, actionable PR descriptions, and precise API docs.
- Impact orientation: prefer changes that improve latency, cost, reliability, or developer experience.

Working model
- Hybrid-friendly: core collaboration hours are 10:00–16:00 local team time. Offices are available in major hubs for team days and recruitment. Remote-first expectations for distributed teams.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy; engineering teams should set coverage expectations for releases and on-call.

2) Roles & career ladders (overview)

This section summarizes level bands and expectations for common functions. For full leveled role guides with competency matrices, see the function-specific pages.

Engineering (Backend / Serving Runtime / Infra / SRE)
- E1 (Entry): contributes to small features and bug fixes, writes tests, follows established patterns.
- E2 (Mid): owns medium-scope features, mentors juniors, participates in design.
- E3 (Senior): leads service-level designs, owns reliability and performance outcomes, influences architecture.
- E4 (Staff): drives cross-service initiatives, sets technical direction, high-impact optimizations (cost/latency).
- E5+ (Principal / Distinguished): company-wide technical leadership, public benchmarks, and external representation.

Product & Design
- P1–P3: individual PM/Designer contributors focusing on feature delivery and user research.
- P4 (Senior PM): drives product area strategy, cross-functional roadmaps, and metrics.
- P5+ (Director/Head): leads multiple product areas or an entire product line.

Applied ML & Research
- M1–M3: model evaluation, prompt engineering, onboarding open models.
- M4: owns model quality frameworks, eval harnesses, and regression triage.

Other noteable ladders: Sales, Customer Success, People Ops, Finance. Each has a separate leveled career document linked in Related pages.

Promotion and calibration process
1. Manager nominates candidate with evidence (impact write-up, PRs, metrics, peer feedback).
2. Panel review: peers + manager review the packet against the leveled rubric.
3. Calibration: senior leaders review across teams for consistency.
4. Outcome communicated within two weeks of nomination.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & financial
- Medical, dental, vision plans with company contribution tiers. Enrollment via HR portal within 30 days of start.
- 401(k) with company match (vesting schedule on HR portal).
- Equity grants: new hires receive RSUs with 4-year vesting and 1-year cliff by default.

Time off & leave
- Flexible PTO (manager-approved). Minimum 15 days/year recommended for planning.
- Parental leave: primary caregivers 16 weeks paid, secondary caregivers 8 weeks paid.
- Care & bereavement leave: see HR portal for policy details.

Development & learning
- $1,500 annual learning stipend for books, conferences, courses.
- Internal conference (Redwood Summit) and monthly brown-bag talks.

Extras and wellbeing
- Commuter/office stipend for those who use co-working or office space.
- Wellness benefits including therapy reimbursements and mental health days.
- Hardware budget on hire and refresh every 36 months.

How to access benefits
- All enrollments and benefits FAQs are available in the HR portal: https://hr.redwood.internal (SSO). For benefits exceptions or accommodations contact people-ops@redwood.com.

4) Hiring process and timelines (standard flow)

High-level stages and expected timelines (typical total cycle: 3–6 weeks)
1. Requisition and sourcing: Hiring manager creates req in Greenhouse and attaches role profile (1–3 days).
2. Screening: Recruiter screens and schedules initial call (1 week).
3. Interview loop: usually 4–6 interviews including a take-home or live exercise for senior ICs (1–2 weeks).
4. Debrief & decision: interviewers submit feedback in Greenhouse; hiring committee review (3–7 days).
5. Offer & negotiation: recruiter extends offer; must include base, equity, and sign-on details.
6. Background check & acceptance: standard checks completed within 3–5 business days.

Interview expectations and rubrics
- Use the company rubric available in Greenhouse. Interviewers should focus on role-specific competencies, coding/design scenarios for engineering, and product sense for PMs.
- All interviewers must submit feedback within 48 hours.

Diversity & inclusive hiring
- All job descriptions must be reviewed by people-ops for inclusive language. Interview panels should include at least one underrepresented group member where practical.

5) New hire onboarding (30-90 day playbook)

Before day 1 (recruiter & manager responsibilities)
- Create onboarding checklist in the Onboard template (People Ops).
- Request access groups in Okta: GH, G Suite, Slack, Payroll, HR Portal, Datadog, PagerDuty, Console, DevSandbox.
- Schedule first-week meetings (intro, team goals, buddy pairing).

Day 1–7 (orientation and access)
1. Orientation session with people-ops: benefits, payroll, security overview.
2. Manager: 1:1 to review priorities, role expectations, and 30/60/90 plan.
3. Buddy: assigned for first 30 days to help with developer workflows and team norms.
4. Access verification: confirm GitHub, Slack, Okta SSO, Console, DevSandbox. Report missing access to helpdesk@redwood.com.

Week 2–4 (ramp and first deliverable)
- Small onboarding project: triaged bug or small feature that touches the team’s CI and runtime. Goal: produce a PR, pass reviews, and get merged.
- Attend required trainings: Security & Data Handling, SLO fundamentals, and Code Review Best Practices.

Month 1–3 (impact ramp)
- 30-day check-in: manager + buddy to confirm access and team's process fit.
- 60-day check-in: progress on first larger project and cross-team collaboration.
- 90-day review: formal onboarding completion, competencies reviewed, and next-level goals set.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Primary systems (access via Okta SSO)
- GitHub (repo access): service ownership is managed through CODEOWNERS and the infra-team. Request repo access via GitHub teams in Okta.
- Slack: #all, #eng, #infra, #people-ops, plus private team channels. Use thread-first communication for async.
- Console (internal Redwood Console): used for per-customer dashboards and model routing configs. Owners: eng-platform@redwood.com.
- DevSandbox: ephemeral developer environments for testing model variants. Request quota via the DevSandbox self-service page.
- PagerDuty: on-call management for infra and runtime teams. Ensure schedule is up to date and escalation policy is visible.
- Datadog & Sentry: observability and error tracking. Dashboards are grouped by service.
- HR Portal: benefits, payroll, time off requests; people-ops manages enrollments.
- Greenhouse: applicant tracking and interview feedback. Recruiters and hiring managers use templates stored in Greenhouse.
- Linear: engineering task tracking for team-level boards. Use labels for routing and priority.

Access requests & troubleshooting
- Standard access: submit an Okta group request. Automations will provision most common apps within 24 hours.
- For escalations (accounts not provisioned after 48 hours) email helpdesk@redwood.com with subject "Onboarding access escalation: <new hire name>". Include manager and buddy in CC.

Tooling owner contacts (examples)
- Okta / SSO: security@redwood.com
- Console: eng-platform@redwood.com
- DevSandbox: infra@redwood.com
- People Ops / HR Portal: people-ops@redwood.com
- PagerDuty & On-call: eng-sre@redwood.com

7) Useful links and resources

Appendix: templates and examples

- Manager nomination template for promotion: Candidate summary, Evidence (PRs, metrics), Peer feedback, Proposed new level and rationale.

Owner & maintenance
- Document owner: people-ops (document steward: Alex Kim).
- Review cadence: annual review in Q2 and ad-hoc updates for policy changes.
- For corrections or feedback open a PR on this Confluence page or email people-ops@redwood.com.

This page aims to be a concise, operational reference. For deeper role-specific detail, promotion rubrics, or legal/benefit plan documents, follow the links in Related pages or contact people-ops.
